section_suggestions.title: Key Relationships
section_suggestions.guidance: Narrative about the most significant relationships. Name each person with a link to their dossier. Explain the nature and significance of each relationship, not just that it exists.

curation.lead:
Boris Nikolic was identified as a scientific adviser in a September 2013 Gates-campus meeting agenda [EFTA02725118]. Released correspondence documents a substantive 2013 backchannel between Nikolic and Jeffrey Epstein during Nikolic's departure from Bill Gates's organization [EFTA00873874][EFTA01966988]. Epstein drafted a message in Nikolic's voice about the exit, and Nikolic replied “this is great” while asking Epstein to hold it until after a possible face-to-face discussion with Gates [EFTA00873874]. A second Epstein draft in Nikolic's voice referred to resignation, marital conflict, and allegations about Gates's private life [EFTA01966988]. Gates later testified that the drafts were never sent, that Epstein made veiled references he experienced as pressure, and that the released records made it seriously probable Epstein contemplated blackmail; Gates expressly denied that Epstein actually blackmailed him [Finding #13236].

On October 23, 2013, Nikolic forwarded Epstein a JPMorgan email and attached biographies for several possible tax and trusts-and-estates advisers, including Loretta A. Ippolito [Finding #13231]. Ippolito had joined Paul Weiss as a partner that July [Finding #13238]. The forwarding proves that Nikolic shared a live adviser-selection packet with Epstein, but the released record does not establish that Ippolito or any other candidate was interviewed or retained [Finding #13239]. Melinda French Gates's 2021 divorce petition separately named Ippolito and Bruce Birenboim of Paul Weiss, but the bounded record review found no personnel or information-flow bridge from the 2013 packet to that later representation [Finding #13225].

sections.title: The 2013 Gates Exit Backchannel
sections.content:
On June 16, 2013, Jeffrey Epstein sent Nikolic a draft beginning “Bill, I am in tears,” written as though Nikolic were addressing Bill Gates [EFTA00873874]. The draft said Nikolic had asked Epstein to oversee and negotiate his departure and had granted Epstein powers covering financial and legal representation [EFTA00873874]. Nikolic replied “this is great,” questioned whether to send it or speak face to face, and asked Epstein to hold the message for eight days [EFTA00873874].

On July 18, 2013, Epstein created another draft in Nikolic's voice that referred to resignation, a marital crisis, and alleged details about Gates's private life [EFTA01966988]. Gates testified that neither draft was sent to him and said one could describe the conduct as attempted blackmail only if the drafts had been sent, which he said did not occur [Finding #13236]. Gates also said Epstein made veiled references that felt like pressure and that the released records made it seriously probable Epstein contemplated blackmail, while denying that Epstein ever completed a blackmail demand [Finding #13236].

The emails establish that Epstein drafted and coordinated at least one proposed exit communication with Nikolic [EFTA00873874]. They do not establish that Nikolic authored every allegation in the drafts, saw the July draft, or agreed to a completed blackmail demand [EFTA00873874][EFTA01966988][Finding #13236].

sections.title: The Adviser Packet Forwarded to Epstein
sections.content:
On October 23, 2013, Nikolic forwarded Epstein a JPMorgan email expressly proposing interviews with three New York trusts-and-estates candidates—William D. Zabel, Loretta A. Ippolito, and Lee Caney—and attaching additional lawyer or adviser biographies for Seth J. Entin, Gabriel F. Hernandez, and Carlos Serrano [Finding #13231][EFTA02709351]. The record does not describe those three additional biography subjects as part of the expressly proposed New York interview slate. The email framed the proposed interviews as a way for Nikolic to decide whom to hire [Finding #13231][EFTA02709351]. The transmission shows that Epstein received material used during a live adviser-selection process, but the packet was a multi-candidate referral rather than an Ippolito-only recommendation and does not establish his participation in interviews or selection [Finding #13231].

Ippolito was already a partner in Paul Weiss's personal representation department when JPMorgan included her biography [Finding #13238]. The firm announcement identified Brad Karp as chair and quoted him welcoming Ippolito, but neither the packet nor the bounded follow-up search documents Karp participating in Nikolic's adviser search [Finding #13238][Finding #13239]. Exact-name, scheduling, engagement, conflict, billing, and alternate-candidate searches found no later public record that Nikolic interviewed or retained Ippolito [Finding #13239].

Melinda French Gates's May 3, 2021 divorce petition named Ippolito and Bruce Birenboim of Paul Weiss as attorneys for the petitioner [Finding #13225]. That later representation is relevant for network tracking, but the current evidence does not connect it to the 2013 packet or show a common personnel or information-flow bridge [Finding #13225][Finding #13239].

sections.title: Gates-Linked Meetings and Investments
sections.content:
In December 2010, Gates emailed Nikolic that he could not attend a dinner with Epstein and wrote that Nathan had agreed with Nikolic that Gates would enjoy meeting him [EFTA02410629]. The message places Nikolic in the routing of an early proposed Gates–Epstein meeting [EFTA02410629].

On September 3, 2013, Gates and Nikolic executed a letter agreement covering Nikolic's interests in Foundation Medicine and ResearchGate, including a payment formula and Nikolic's observer role at Foundation Medicine [EFTA02685163]. On September 11, 2013, an agenda for an International Peace Institute meeting at the Gates campus listed Nikolic as “Scientific Advisor” among participants discussing a polio-eradication proposal [EFTA02725118]. These documents establish Nikolic's working access to Gates-linked investment and philanthropic processes during the same year as the exit drafts and adviser packet [EFTA02685163][EFTA02725118].

sections.title: Third-Party Information and Introductions
sections.content:
Nikolic sent Epstein World Economic Forum participant lists in January 2011 and January 2013, with the 2013 message asking Epstein to identify anyone Nikolic should meet [EFTA02686104][EFTA02686168][EFTA02707383]. In June 2015, Nikolic told Epstein that his next email would introduce Ilya Ponomarev, whom he described as a member of the Russian Duma [EFTA02360267].

Several messages also place Nikolic between Epstein and Kimbal Musk: a September 2012 invitation was routed through Nikolic, a February 2013 divorce update was relayed by Nikolic to Epstein, and an April 2017 message from TED told Epstein that Kimbal and Elon Musk were present [EFTA02560007][EFTA02358398]. An August 2013 logistics email from Lesley Groff gave Nikolic Epstein's aircraft tail number and said Karyna Shuliak could update him on timing [EFTA02336502]. The records document recurring transmission of names, schedules, introductions, and third-party updates; they do not by themselves establish why Nikolic shared each item or what Epstein did with it [EFTA02686104][EFTA02360267][EFTA02560007][EFTA02336502].

sections.title: The 1953 Trust Designation
sections.content: The 1953 Trust instrument executed on August 8, 2019 named Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn as trustees and placed Nikolic first in the succession list for a vacancy [EFTA01266204]. The instrument then named Barnaby Marsh, Anthony Barrett, Kathryn Ruemmler, David Mitchell, Steve Hanson, and Eva Dubin in successive order [EFTA01266204]. The instrument documents the designation but does not explain why Epstein placed Nikolic first, whether Nikolic knew in advance, or whether he consented [EFTA01266204].

curation.system_role: Former Gates science adviser whose released correspondence documents an Epstein backchannel around proposed exit communications, adviser-selection materials, Gates-linked projects, and third-party contacts [EFTA00873874][Finding #13231]. A 2019 trust instrument also placed Nikolic first in its successor-trustee order without explaining the choice [EFTA01266204].
open_questions: Do later messages, calendars, or call records show what Nikolic and Epstein discussed after the June and July 2013 exit drafts [EFTA00873874][EFTA01966988]?

Do JPMorgan calendars, interview schedules, conflict checks, engagement letters, or billing records identify which adviser candidates Nikolic contacted after the October 23, 2013 packet [Finding #13231][Finding #13239]?
Can any primary record identify who initiated the adviser search or why Nikolic forwarded the full candidate packet to Epstein [EFTA02709351]?
Do contemporaneous records explain how Ippolito and Birenboim came to represent Melinda French Gates in 2021, independently of the presently unconnected 2013 packet [Finding #13225]?
Do trust-drafting communications explain why Nikolic was placed first in the 1953 Trust succession list or whether he knew of the designation before execution [EFTA01266204]?

citation_findings.summary: SYSTEMIC PATTERN: The May 3, 2021 Gates divorce petition names Bruce Birenboim and Loretta Ippolito of Paul, Weiss for Melinda French Gates; the two lawyers' located Epstein-release occurrences are unrelated, role-consistent 2013 and 2016 matters, and no common-personnel or information-flow bridge to the divorce was found.
citation_findings.detail: Page 4 of King County Superior Court case 21-3-02273-1 SEA lists Birenboim and Ippolito as attorneys for petitioner; Brad Karp is not named. The exact-name search across all six configured corpora returned five Kabass hits that deduplicated to two events, two LMSBAND duplicates, and zero Unified email/document, House 20K, FBI, or reporting results. In October 2013, JPMorgan sent Boris Nikolic biographies for Ippolito and two other New York trusts-and-estates lawyers as possible interview candidates; Nikolic forwarded the package to Epstein, but the page does not mention Bill Gates, Melinda Gates, divorce, a hiring, or any communication with Ippolito. In March 2016, Birenboim stated an internal Paul Weiss escrow policy in a Leon Black matter; Karp later forwarded the response to Epstein. The negative result is scoped to configured corpora and does not prove that private or undisclosed contacts never occurred.
citation_findings.target_name: Melinda French Gates / Paul, Weiss representation

citation_findings.detail: Separate 2026 testimony layer; it does not establish a Karp or Paul Weiss role in the pressure episode and should not be conflated with the 2014 Gates-related DAF consultation. Each evidence row below is a continuous verbatim passage with a transcript line anchor.

evidence.source_quote: If those emails that contained some truth and some false things were ever sent, then we could say there was an attempt at blackmail. That never happened. You know, I don't know if Dr. Nikolic ever saw those, but I certainly never saw those. Those would have been -- then it would have been black and white that that's what they were attempting to do. What actually happened is they made veiled references that, because of that, you know, I explicitly raised the idea that their disclosing whatever they knew about me, that I would deal with that, and I was not going to raise the offer because of my concerns about what might be behind those veiled references.

No, he never sent me anything that I would call blackmail. As I've said, he made veiled references to things like we should all want to be friends. Now that I see the January release of documents, it appears that in many cases he, at least in emails to himself, was sort of rehearsing how either he or he coaching someone else might choose to blackmail me, but none of those messages were ever sent to me. You know, I never paid Jeffrey Epstein anything. And so it's a bit speculation, but the different things are quite consistent that he would encourage others to try and give him leverage over me, but then that never came to pass.
He never blackmailed me, but looking at these emails, it raises a serious probability that he contemplated blackmailing me.

citation_findings.summary: Loretta Ippolito was already a Paul, Weiss partner before the October 2013 Nikolic candidate packet: the firm announced on July 3, 2013 that she had joined as a partner in its personal representation department in New York.
citation_findings.detail: The firm announcement identifies Brad S. Karp as chair and quotes him welcoming Ippolito. This establishes her firm and practice context when JPMorgan later included her biography in the October 23, 2013 candidate packet; it does not establish that Nikolic interviewed or retained her.

citation_findings.summary: Bounded retention test: the released record shows JPMorgan offering to arrange interviews with several candidate lawyers, but exact-name, alias, scheduling, engagement, conflict, billing, and alternate-candidate searches found no later public record that Boris Nikolic interviewed or retained Loretta Ippolito.
citation_findings.detail: Coverage: all six brad-karp corpora (Kabasshouse, Unified emails/docs, LMSBAND, House Oversight, FBI, reporting), exact candidate-name searches for William Zabel, Lee Caney, Seth Entin, Gabriel Hernandez, Carlos Serrano, Joanne Johnson and Mayer Brown, plus targeted CourtListener, SEC EDGAR, IRS 990, unified registry and official Paul, Weiss/Wayback checks. The three packet hits EFTA00632249, EFTA01189736 and EFTA02709351 are duplicate renderings of one October 23, 2013 email, not corroboration. No later interview, scheduling, conflict, engagement, billing, direct Ippolito-Nikolic communication, or documented selection of another candidate was located. This bounded negative result cannot exclude private engagement records that were never made public or released.
